clue.text: Low character: English pound flagging

parts.note: a colon is a punctuation character
lb is the abbreviation for a pound in weight

explanation.surface: A lowly fellow, and the English pound is losing value.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character' works twice: it ends the definition and also supplies the punctuation mark. David Low was a cartoonist whose pompous reactionary creation was COLONEL BLIMP.
explanation.definitionFit: The blustering old officer was the famous creation of the cartoonist David Low, so he is literally Low's character.

clue.text: Is not able to get to grips with a South American card game

indicators.note: to get to grips with something is to grasp it, so the outer word holds the following letters

explanation.surface: Someone who cannot cope with a South American card game.
explanation.walkthrough: The first word reads as part of the phrase but is only a link; 'a South' goes inside the word for unable, then 'American' tacks on the final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Canasta is a rummy-style card game that originated in Uruguay.

clue.text: No end of cash — lie back and relax!

indicators.note: 'no end' asks for the last letter of the following word to be dropped

parts.note: lolly is British slang for money

explanation.surface: Penniless, so there is nothing to do but recline and unwind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No end of cash' sounds like plenty of money, but it means the slang word for cash with its last letter cut.
explanation.definitionFit: To loll is to lounge or sprawl lazily, which is reclining at ease.

clue.text: Stick up landlady on vacation, memorably

indicators.note: in a down entry, 'up' means the word is written from bottom to top
a word on vacation has been emptied, so only its two outermost letters stay

parts.note: first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A landlady going off on holiday was memorably held up at gunpoint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stick up' looks like a robbery but is a stick turned upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: Notably and memorably both describe something done in a remarkable, worth-noting way.

clue.text: Roped in girl to go over dictionary

explanation.surface: A young woman was recruited to check over a dictionary.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry one piece going over another means it sits above it.
explanation.definitionFit: To lasso is to catch with a rope loop, so a lassoed animal has been roped in.

clue.text: Billions put away by ex-Labour leader in hideaway

indicators.note: something put away is removed from view, so that letter is taken out

parts.note: Tony Blair, former Labour Prime Minister

explanation.surface: Billions stashed by a former Labour leader in a secret retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: A lair is an animal's den, and by extension any secret hiding place.

clue.text: One Day International cricket initially bores mother a bit

indicators.note: to bore is to drill into something, so these letters go inside
'initially' asks for just the opening letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: One-day cricket rather bores my mother.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket abbreviation and one letter sit inside MUM, mother.
explanation.definitionFit: A modicum is a small quantity, which is what a bit is.

clue.text: Modelling PVC material, an Avenger

indicators.note: modelling means shaping, so the following letters are moulded into a new form

explanation.surface: A superhero posing in a plastic costume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'an' looks like part of the definition but belongs to the letters being rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Captain Marvel is a Marvel Comics superhero and member of the Avengers team.

clue.text: We all go out on this brass hat's three-wheeler

definitions.text: We all go out on this

parts.note: a brass hat is a senior officer such as a general; plus the possessive S

explanation.surface: Everyone heads out for a ride on a senior officer's tricycle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go out' means stop work, as in a walkout. A brass hat is British slang for a high-ranking officer.
explanation.definitionFit: In a general strike workers across every industry walk out together, so all go out.

clue.text: Ring to cancel Spielberg classic

parts.note: E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial, Steven Spielberg's film

explanation.surface: Phone round to call off a screening of a Spielberg film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' looks like a verb about telephoning; it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: An annulet is a small ring, especially as a moulding on a column or in heraldry.

clue.text: Slender rod daughter left embedded in small conifer

indicators.note: something embedded is set firmly inside another thing

parts.note: a pine is a conifer; the outer part

explanation.surface: A thin pole the daughter left stuck in a little fir tree.
explanation.walkthrough: S plus the tree name forms the outer shell, with the two single letters sitting inside the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A spindle is a thin rod on which thread is wound or that turns as an axle.

clue.text: Intros from The Apprentice, Sugar's key assignment

indicators.note: intros are introductions, the opening letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: The opening scenes of The Apprentice show Lord Sugar setting the vital challenge.
explanation.walkthrough: The Apprentice is a British TV contest hosted by businessman Alan Sugar, where candidates are set a weekly challenge.
explanation.definitionFit: A task is a piece of work given to someone, an assignment.

clue.text: One's read caution after illegal drug

indicators.note: after says the piece named before it is placed second, behind the piece that follows

parts.note: to book a footballer is to caution them

explanation.surface: Someone is warned after being caught with drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's read' sounds like a reading of a person; it means a thing that is read. A referee who books a player gives a caution.
explanation.definitionFit: An e-book is an electronic text intended to be read on a screen.

clue.text: Ms Reeves's boundless longing

indicators.note: without bounds means the outer edges of the name are cut away

explanation.surface: The Chancellor's endless yearning.
explanation.walkthrough: Rachel Reeves is the British Chancellor of the Exchequer; drop her first name's first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An ache is a persistent yearning, as in to ache for something.

clue.text: Cathedral city set up Socialist Times

indicators.note: in a down entry, set up means raised from bottom to top

parts.note: by means times, as in three by four

explanation.surface: A cathedral city establishes a left-wing newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Socialist Times' looks like a newspaper title. Derby is an English city in the Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Derby has a cathedral and was granted city status, so it is a cathedral city.

clue.text: Philosopher seen in Polyanthos regularly

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: first, third, fifth, seventh and ninth letters

explanation.surface: A thinker regularly spotted among the primulas.
explanation.walkthrough: A polyanthus is a garden primula; the plural shown is an alternative form.
explanation.definitionFit: Plato was the ancient Greek thinker, pupil of Socrates.

clue.text: Buccaneer, after losing head, discharged lackey with fury

indicators.note: losing the head means the first letter is dropped
a discharged word has had its contents unloaded, so only its edges remain

explanation.surface: A pirate, after being beheaded, angrily dismissed a servant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' reads as a beheading, but just removes the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Irately means angrily, so it describes acting in fury.

clue.text: Cover flipping novel predicament

indicators.note: flipping something over turns it round

explanation.surface: A wretched book jacket is a real problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' looks like a mild British swear word attached to the novel; it is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilemma is a difficult choice between options, a predicament.

clue.text: Camera panned around front of battlefield — gruesome

indicators.note: around places the other letters on either side
panned means harshly criticised or swung about, so the letters are jumbled
the front of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A camera sweeping across a battlefield shows horrors.
explanation.definitionFit: Macabre means dwelling on death, ghastly or gruesome.

clue.text: Tuchel's earning cups here?

parts.note: letters that straddle the two words

explanation.surface: Is this where the German coach is winning trophies?
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Tuchel managed the London football club and won the Champions League there in 2021; the club's name sits inside his name and the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: Chelsea is the London football club where Tuchel won major trophies, so the whole clue points to it.

clue.text: Quick! Train former journos!

parts.note: a second pointer to the whole word, as in a fast train; it supplies no letters

explanation.surface: Hurry! Coach some ex-reporters!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' also points at the answer, as a fast train; the Express is also a British newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Express means fast, as in express delivery or an express train.

clue.text: Sees two West End musicals, missing endings

indicators.note: missing endings means each word loses its last letter

parts.note: Chess, the musical by the ABBA writers

explanation.surface: Takes in two London shows but leaves before the finale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two' asks for two shows; the West End is London's theatre district.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch a show or a glimpse is to see it, so catches can mean sees.

clue.text: Belt and outfit

definitions.meaning: second meaning: British slang for clothes and gear

explanation.walkthrough: 'Belt' looks like an item of clothing that belongs with 'outfit'; it is the verb, to strike.
explanation.definitionFit: To clobber is to batter someone, and clobber is also informal British slang for clothing or kit.

clue.text: Journalist having base in New York East Side borough

indicators.note: in places one letter inside the abbreviation that follows

parts.note: e is the base of natural logarithms

explanation.surface: A reporter based in New York's East Side district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East Side' looks like Manhattan; it is the east side of London, where Hackney is a borough.
explanation.definitionFit: Hackney is a London borough in the east of the city.

clue.text: Regretted being coarse on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio, words are heard rather than read

explanation.surface: Someone was sorry for swearing on air.
explanation.definitionFit: To rue is to regret, so rued is past-tense regretted.

clue.text: Second professional golf kid

parts.note: G is golf in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A second golf pro is just a kid.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprog is British slang for a small child.

clue.text: Hollywood gong ignoring old Cliff

indicators.note: ignoring means leaving out, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: an Oscar is a film award

explanation.surface: A film award passed over a veteran named Cliff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cliff' looks like a name, as with the singer Cliff Richard; it is the rock face. A gong is British slang for an award.
explanation.definitionFit: A scar is a steep rocky crag or cliff face on a hillside.

clue.text: Tech saving lives of, for starters, Hamilton, Alonso, Leclerc & Ocon

indicators.note: starters are the opening parts, so each name gives its first letter

explanation.surface: The safety device that protected four Formula One drivers.
explanation.walkthrough: The four names are Formula One drivers, and the device is the cockpit protection bar fitted to their cars.
explanation.definitionFit: The halo is the curved titanium bar over an F1 cockpit, credited with saving drivers' lives in crashes.

clue.text: Air force served up eastern food

indicators.note: in a down entry, served up means presented from the bottom upwards

explanation.surface: The air force dished out oriental cuisine.
explanation.definitionFit: Fare is the food and drink offered, as in simple country fare.

clue.text: Force to work in gentlemen's lav — eww!

indicators.note: in says the letters lie within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Made to clean a disgusting men's toilet.
explanation.walkthrough: Lav is British slang for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: To enslave someone is to compel them into unpaid servitude, forcing them to work.

clue.text: Fifties bohemian from best family from the east

indicators.note: in an across entry, reading from the east means right to left

explanation.surface: A 1950s free spirit descended from a prominent eastern family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'best' looks like an adjective; it is the verb, to defeat.
explanation.definitionFit: Beatniks were the bohemian youth of the 1950s Beat Generation.

clue.text: Drive adopted by former PM: railway operation on a large scale

parts.note: John Major, ex-Prime Minister, with possessive S

explanation.surface: An ex-premier's big push on railways is a huge undertaking.
explanation.walkthrough: A drive adopted by Major is Major's urge. 'operation' looks like a business venture; it is medical.
explanation.definitionFit: Major surgery is a serious, extensive surgical operation, so literally an operation on a large scale.
